clue.text: Make some 14, say...

definitions.note: the definition is the run-on clue in 10, an example of the whole phrase

blocks.note: to mull wine is to heat and spice it, making mulled wine
mulled wine is an example of a tipple, an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: An instruction to brew up a batch of mulled wine, trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Clues 1, 5, 9 and 10 run on as one: the 'heartless' in 5 also works here, each word losing one of its doubled middle letters. Together the four lights make MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTION, defined by the tally clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiple is the first word of the phrase multiple choice question, a test format offering several possible answers.

clue.text: Titled gentleman losing right to go underground

indicators.note: losing something means it is removed from the word

blocks.note: a marquis is a nobleman ranking above an earl
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A nobleman giving up his rights and fleeing into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: to take to the maquis was to join the French wartime resistance and go underground.
explanation.definitionFit: The maquis were the French resistance fighters of World War II, who operated in secret, so the word stands for going into hiding.

clue.text: Shelter on the road to be made up?

blocks.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
a way is a road; on places it after

explanation.surface: A traveller looking for cover beside the road before the journey can continue.
explanation.walkthrough: One speaks of having leeway to make up, meaning lost ground to recover.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is lost time or progress that must be recovered, as a ship drifting off course must catch up.

clue.text: Know at once that resident of 21 land keeps time

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside

blocks.note: clue 21 is FROZEN; the Inuit live in the Arctic
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An Arctic dweller who keeps time by instinct.
explanation.walkthrough: IN(T)UIT: the time abbreviation goes after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To intuit is to understand something instinctively without reasoning, so the knowledge arrives immediately.

clue.text: Privy page follows new duke to be respected

indicators.note: a new version of the following word has its letters rearranged

blocks.note: a privy is a lavatory, the loo in British slang
these letters are rearranged
standard abbreviation; follows puts it after
taken as written

explanation.surface: A page boy waiting on a newly made duke, a figure to be held in esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Privy' looks like an adjective (private) but it is a toilet. The definition should be read as 'respected', with 'be' linking.
explanation.definitionFit: To be looked up to is to be admired and held in high regard, the same as being respected.

clue.text: ...with heartless 22 15...

definitions.note: the definition is the run-on clue in 10, an example of the whole phrase

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter of the item is cut out

blocks.note: coated ice cream suggests a choc ice, an ice cream bar covered in chocolate

explanation.surface: A continuation of the opening clue, adding a chocolate-coated ice cream to the hot drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A choc ice is a British ice cream bar coated in chocolate. Its middle C goes; this light is the second word of MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Choice is the middle word of the phrase for a test where candidates pick one answer among several options.

clue.text: Ranch house had a nice aspect

indicators.note: a new aspect is a changed appearance, so the letters take a new form

blocks.note: these eight letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ranch house enjoying a pleasant outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large estate or its main house in Spanish-speaking countries, like a ranch homestead.

clue.text: I like this theme; it's concerned with what might be radioactive

definitions.text: concerned with what might be radioactive

blocks.note: taken as written
so means in this way
a theme is a topic

explanation.surface: Someone praising a subject that turns out to be about nuclear physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotopic relates to isotopes, atomic variants of an element, some of which are unstable and emit radiation.

clue.text: Risk bad feeling after conclusion

blocks.note: an end is a conclusion
anger is bad feeling; after places it second

explanation.surface: Resentment lingering once something is over is a hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger is to put something in peril, which is what risking it means as a verb.

clue.text: ...and 20 for self-reversal? - ???...

blocks.note: clue 20 is SEARCH, and a quest is a search
read backwards, these letters say NO I: a refusal of the self

explanation.surface: The chain of clues goes on, asking for a search and a turnaround of oneself, followed by a row of query marks.
explanation.walkthrough: The three question marks are the definition: they literally depict what the word names. The second half is loose: I is the self, and ION backwards spells NO I.
explanation.definitionFit: A question mark is the punctuation that ends an inquiry, so three of them stand for the noun naming such an inquiry.

clue.text: ...Tally - is it A, B, C or D? Not B, C

indicators.note: telling the solver to put one letter in place of the one that is ruled out

blocks.note: the letters and the word or read straight through

explanation.surface: A multiple-choice paper asking a candidate which option tallies, with the hint that B and C are wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not B, C' reads as 'C, not B': swap the B for a C. The clue is also the definition of the whole chain, a typical multiple choice question.
explanation.definitionFit: To tally is to agree or correspond, and accord means agreement, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Dine out, entertaining three kings in a dream

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their usual order
to entertain is to take guests inside, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: the three wise men of the nativity story, often called kings
these four letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dining out with three royal guests, which sounds too good to be true.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magi are the wise men of the nativity, traditionally called the three kings.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imagined exists only in the mind, the way things in a dream do, so the phrase works as a loose adjectival equivalent.

clue.text: Answer: cancel resignation?

blocks.note: first meaning: to reply, especially sharply
second meaning, read as join again: someone who resigned and then signs back up

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading, splitting the word into RE- (again) and JOIN.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to reply or retort, and literally it means become a member once more after leaving.

clue.text: Unskilled group circulating changed locale

indicators.note: circulating means moving round, so the letters are mixed
changed means altered in order

blocks.note: a club is a group of members
the word as printed, but the parse needs an R where it has a C: the setter's slip

explanation.surface: A workforce moving around a district that has changed.
explanation.walkthrough: The likeliest reading is a jumble of a word for group with LOCALE, but CLUB plus LOCALE has a second C where the answer needs R: a setter's slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-collar describes manual workers, and is used loosely of unskilled or semi-skilled labour.

clue.text: Hot drink for Northumbrian king held by German 26 endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped
something held by another sits inside its grasp

blocks.note: clue 26 is a miller, and Müller is German for miller as well as a common surname
Edwin was a seventh-century king of Northumbria

explanation.surface: An Anglo-Saxon king offered a warming drink by a German host.
explanation.walkthrough: The German for miller is Müller; the umlaut is ignored and its last letter drops before the king goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Mulled wine is red wine heated with sugar and spices, served warm, so it is a classic example of a hot drink.

clue.text: Diamonds for the elite that's sweet and 21

blocks.note: ice is slang for diamonds
the cream is the best part

explanation.surface: Gems for high society, something sweet and frosty.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue 21 is FROZEN, so the definition is a sweet frozen thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice cream is a sweetened frozen dessert made from dairy, matching sweet and very cold.

clue.text: Doctor with feudal manner - appalling!

indicators.note: a manner is a way of arranging, so the letters are put in a new way

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
these six letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medic behaving like a medieval lord, which is shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadful and appalling both mean extremely bad or shocking, so they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Plan for audience you'll shed when the order's changed

indicators.note: an audience listens, so the words are taken as heard

blocks.note: said first once the two words swap places
said second

explanation.surface: A warning that you will lose some listeners if you change the running order.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the two words to 'shed you'll' and say them: that is the British pronunciation, shed-yool.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule is a timetable or programme of intended events, the noun for a plan.

clue.text: Fellow sailors on boat, chiropodist and harvester?

blocks.note: co- is the prefix for a fellow, as in co-worker
the Royal Navy
a cutter is a small sailing vessel; on means placed after the previous letters

explanation.surface: A list of crewmen aboard a vessel, oddly joined by a foot specialist and a farmhand.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on both senses: a corn is a hard patch on the foot, which an old-fashioned chiropodist cut, and a harvester literally cuts corn.
explanation.definitionFit: A corn-cutter was an old name for a person who pared foot calluses, and could jokingly describe someone reaping grain.

clue.text: Permit includes transport to Near East

indicators.note: to include is to take inside

blocks.note: to let is to allow
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A travel permit allowing transport to the eastern Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: LE(VAN)T.
explanation.definitionFit: The Levant is the historic name for the countries of the eastern Mediterranean coast, the region once called the Near East.

clue.text: Try to find and brand the church

blocks.note: to brand is to burn a mark, to sear
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Seeking out the church and stamping a mark on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To search is to look carefully for something, which is what trying to locate it means.

clue.text: Away with Buddhism! It's very cold

blocks.note: as in to and fro, fro meaning away
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: Someone dismissing Buddhism as a chilly faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen describes something turned to ice or extremely chilly, so it fits an intense level of coldness.

clue.text: Tucked in to fish, partly dressed

indicators.note: the eating is put to, that is into, the item that follows

blocks.note: to tuck in is to eat heartily
a common sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone tucking in to a fish supper while not fully clothed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucked in' means ate heartily, not folded away; 'partly dressed' suggests half-clothed but means covered on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Coated means covered with a layer, such as breadcrumbs or a sauce dressing a dish, so only the surface is dressed.

clue.text: Refrain about English ancestor

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: to forbear is to hold back or refrain
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A song's chorus about something English, or someone holding back from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' looks like a noun, a chorus, but it is the verb meaning hold back.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is someone from whom you are descended, a person from an earlier generation of your family.

clue.text: Swear at light's flowing out

blocks.note: to eff is to swear, from the euphemism for a certain four-letter word
lux is the unit of illumination, Latin for light; at places it next

explanation.surface: Someone cursing at a lamp as it pours out its glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eff and blind' is British slang for swearing.
explanation.definitionFit: An efflux is an outward flow of liquid or gas, so the phrase describes the noun's action fairly.

clue.text: Prison for Miss Philips, back holding head of loved pet

indicators.note: going back means the name is read from right to left
holding means wrapping around what follows
the head is the first letter of the following word

blocks.note: Zara Phillips, the Princess Royal's daughter and an Olympic equestrian
only the opening letter of this word is kept
a typical household pet

explanation.surface: A princess's daughter returning from a trip with her beloved animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue spells the surname with one L; the royal is Zara Phillips, daughter of Princess Anne.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcatraz was a notorious federal penitentiary on an island in San Francisco Bay, so it is a well-known example of a jail.

clue.text: Runner, about 50, could use a stone

indicators.note: about means around, so one item encloses the other

blocks.note: a miler is an athlete running the one-mile race
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An athlete around fifty who might shed some weight, a stone being a British unit of fourteen pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The stone is a millstone, not a weight: MIL(L)ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A miller grinds grain between millstones, so a stone is the essential tool of that trade.

clue.text: German girl with information about attempt to throw up

indicators.note: about means around, so the first item surrounds the second

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
to retch is to heave as if vomiting

explanation.surface: A girl from Germany with news about someone trying to be sick.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang, short for general information.
explanation.definitionFit: Gretchen is a typical German female name, a pet form of Margarete, famously Faust's love in Goethe.
